minutes.headline: Committee kept rewriting a staff space-needs survey for reusing the Ritter building, no decision on new building
minutes.summary: The Building Design Committee spent nearly the whole meeting line-by-line rewriting a detailed questionnaire for department heads about staffing, space, storage, technology and accessibility needs, meant to test whether the town can reuse the Ritter building rather than build new, per the town manager's direction. No figures or votes on the building itself were taken; the committee agreed to have the chair revise the draft, send it to the town manager, and set the next meeting for March 30.

attendees.role: committee member; self-identified as a department head

votes.outcome: passed, described by the chair as six eyes and three abstains
passed, roll call all in favor

budget_items.topic: PACC (public access TV) finances and possible Town Hall space
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said PACC's Comcast franchise-fee revenue is declining while costs rise, so it is spending down savings and cannot afford rent at a possible Fitchburg TV facility. The committee suggested tabling any decision about giving PACC space in a renovated Town Hall until PACC reviews its own long-term business plan with the town manager.

budget_items.topic: Department budget prep as context for staffing questions
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted that every department head had just been through budget preparation, so questions about current and projected staffing levels should be fresh in their minds and easy to answer.

decisions.decision: No public comment was available this meeting; committee members instead discussed anticipated public feedback and the need for an aggressive engagement effort once a plan exists.
Keep language framing the goal as accessibility for all, not just minimum ADA compliance, in the intro to the department questionnaire.
Avoid stating a specific future population figure (e.g. 20,000) in questionnaire framing; instead ask departments a conditional 'what if population grows' style question.
Strike the proposed question about the town's natural-disaster/business-continuity plan; the committee agreed that is not its job to define.
Table further discussion of PACC/TCP studio relocation and Town Hall space until the committee talks with the town manager.
Send the finished questionnaire to the town manager first and let her decide whether/how to disseminate it to department heads, rather than the committee sending it directly.

Chair will revise the questionnaire, circulate it to members individually (not reply-all, to avoid Open Meeting Law issues) for comment, then bring a final version to the town manager before the next meeting.
Next meeting set for March 30 because the Planning Board has the meeting room on March 16 and March 23.

what_happened.line: Committee spent the meeting rewriting a staff space-needs questionnaire to test reusing the Ritter building, per the town manager's order to rule out reuse before new construction.
No vote or figure on the building itself was taken; the chair will revise the questionnaire and send it to the town manager first.
The town manager, not the committee, will decide whether and how to send the questionnaire to department heads.
Discussion of moving PACC's TV studio or Town Hall storage into a renovated building was tabled pending PACC's own review of its finances with the town manager.
Next meeting set for March 30 because the Planning Board holds the meeting room on March 16 and 23.

why_it_matters: This questionnaire will shape what staffing and space needs get presented to the town manager, feeding into any eventual building or renovation request residents vote on.
Whether the town reuses the Ritter building or builds new affects the size and cost of any future capital request.
PACC's space in a renovated Town Hall depends on its own finances, which the committee says are strained by falling franchise-fee revenue.
